title: Check order
statement: Orders the check rows for a run and for the reference: Lathe's checks by position, then each product's by position, so a product check never changes which of Lathe's problems are found.

title: Space look and place
statement: A product's icon MUST be its `icon` field when that is one emoji or up to two characters, and otherwise its ID as a monogram. Its color MUST be its `color` field when that is a hex color or a color name, and otherwise one derived from its ID, the same on every visit. Spaces MUST be in the products' ID order everywhere they are listed, and the nth space MUST be the one Alt+n opens.

title: Current space
statement: The current space MUST be the product of the page on screen when it belongs to one (its product, domain, record or group page, or its Checks page); on a page outside every space (the products, the format, Settings) it MUST stay the space last chosen, or the first product.

title: Folder placement
statement: Places a product's records in the nav's tree, read by the nav, the domain page, the group pages and the graph alike (DR19). A product holds Shared (its patterns and standards, and each record with no owner, a value object, view, integration or UI component, that two or more domains use, or none, with what sits under it), then its domains, then its open questions. A record with no owner that one domain uses sits in that domain, in its kind's stage and folder, as the store places it (`LA-PLT-UC01-R05`). A domain holds its five stages in the schema's order, `schema.stages`, each named by its own label, then its open questions. A record sits in its kind's stage: at the top of the stage when its parent is its domain or of another stage, or it has none (a flow under its use case, a handler under its command, a test under its obligation, a view), and under its parent when the parent is of the same stage, reached through it (DR21). A kind in no stage gets a folder of its own after the stages. Within a stage, kinds come in the schema's order (Test plan's ten test kinds in the plan's order), and records with a `position` (capabilities, flow steps) come by it, then by ID, with the records outside any capability last. A stage with only one folder (counting empty ones that can start a branch there) holds that folder's records itself: the folder is no level and has no address (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`). An empty stage or kind group is never shown.

title: Graph tree
statement: The graph's tree is the nav's tree, from DS03: the product, its Shared, then its domains, each holding its five stages, their kind groups (none in a stage with one folder, which holds that folder's records itself) and the records in them. A kind group is derived from its parent and the kind of its children, never a record: it has no ID of its own, only its address, and no record links to it.

title: Tree map layout
statement: Each product MUST have a graph of its own: its tree laid out off the main thread, and again only when what it reads (its tree, its labels, the text measure) changes, as one icicle with the product as its single root, then its Shared folder (its own stages), its domains, their stages, folders and records and their children, as the nav's tree has them (`LA-EXP-DS04`). No node, link, hint or minimap box of another product MAY be in it; a record no product reaches is the root of a map of its own. A node's size MUST come from the tree alone, top-down from the product's fixed box (`LA-EXP-DS06`), never from what is in focus: the product's box is as wide as it is tall; a parent's children split its height equally, a gap apart of a tenth of each one's part, their stack filling it from its top edge to its bottom edge, in the tree's order; and a parent's children form a column of their own, all as wide as each other: 0.4 times their parent's width, but never wider than 6 times their own height, so the more children share a parent, the narrower their column, and no box is flatter than 6 to 1. Each column starts a gap of 0.15 times its width after its parent. Each label is centered in its box. Each parent line MUST be drawn level, at the child's middle, from the parent's outline to the child's. Nothing in the map is ever laid out again or resized while the person walks it; filters hide nodes without moving the rest. In the graph, every record or group with the same parent MUST sit in the same column, whatever its kind, so no sibling is further left or further right than another. A column is a depth in the parent/child tree around the focus; within a column, siblings MUST stay together, ordered by their parent's place, then by kind, then by ID. The same specs MUST always give the same map, and the same focus, depth and filters the same framed picture, so walking the graph is predictable: records in one column keep their order, and their places, whatever is in focus. When the data changes, a change under a parent MUST re-lay only that parent's region (for a move, the old and the new parent's; `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R22`): a parent's box is fixed before its children are split, so every box outside the region keeps its place, size and text scale, and existing siblings keep their order.

title: Label fitting
statement:
One rule MUST size every layout of the graph (Tree and Nested), top-down from one fixed product box: siblings are the same size, with the same text. The product's box MUST have a fixed size, the same for every product (300,000 map units), and each parent MUST split its room equally among its children, in the tree's order. Record counts and titles MUST size no box: a busy sibling packs its children smaller, and a quiet one has blank space. How each layout splits its room is `LA-EXP-DS05` (Tree) and `LA-EXP-DS07` (Nested).

A node's label is part of the map. A box's text scale MUST be at most a fixed share of its box's size, the same share at every depth: in the Tree its width over 250 map units (siblings share one width, as `LA-EXP-DS05` sets it from their height); in Nested its side over 400 map units. Siblings MUST share one text scale: the largest, at most that share, at which every sibling's whole label fits its room, its kind and ID line and its title wrapped on whole words, with its padding, its marks, its shape's room and its border. So a framed box's header reads at about the same size on screen (in the Tree within a fifth of each other) whichever box is framed in its own frame (a focus whose children would draw under 11 pixels is framed by their column and reads larger, `LA-EXP-DS09`), and very small boxes have very small text, read by zooming in. Its title, its kind and ID line, its padding and its problem badge MUST grow by that scale, in map units, whatever the person's text size; its border, outline and parent line's stroke grow with it too (never below half in the Nested view), so a box's edge stays in proportion to its label. The text MUST never change size relative to its box: not when the focus changes, not when the camera zooms or settles; only the camera changes how big it looks. Every drawn box carries its label at that size; a box whose title would be drawn under 5 pixels on screen is drawn as a plain block (`LA-EXP-DS10`, `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`). Text is always whole: a box only partly inside the open space (cut by a floating panel, the nav or the wiki card, or by the canvas's edge) MUST draw its label within the visible part of its content box and its side padding less twice its border (inside the box's one fill, never across its edge or its shape's decoration), keeping its own padding at its own scale, as a sticky header stays in view, laid out anew for that part's width, wrapped on whole words, at no larger a scale than its own and centered in it; when it cannot fit there with its title at 9 pixels it MUST NOT be drawn at all, nor its mark or badge. A focused box MUST never be left without its label: where the panels leave its visible part too narrow to hold it, the camera moves, at the same zoom, as little as it takes for it to fit. No label is ever drawn half cut, on any stage.

A title MUST wrap on whole words, after a space, never cut off or ended with an ellipsis; only a word too wide for a line on its own MAY break: after a hyphen or, in a code identifier, after its punctuation (`.`, `_`, `:`, `/`, `(`) or between its camelCase words, and the text scale never lets that happen in a map. The kind and ID line MAY wrap between words; an ID MUST never break across lines. Lines MUST be broken when the map is built, measured by the canvas's own text metrics in the label's faces once they have loaded (the theme's body and mono faces), and the canvas MUST draw exactly those lines in those faces, so the map is laid out again only when its labels, its tree or its faces change, and is the same every time for a given face. Each line's height MUST be in proportion to its text, so no glyph is clipped. Map units MUST be kept in doubles, never rounded, so the deepest boxes keep their places however small they are against the product's box.

title: Nested map layout
statement:
In the Nested view the graph MUST lay out the same tree as the Tree view (`LA-EXP-DS04`), its product's alone with the product as its single root and nothing of another product, once per load of the specs, as nested squares, top-down from the product's fixed square by `LA-EXP-DS06`'s rule: siblings are the same size, with the same text. A parent's room under its header band, inside its padding, MUST hold its children as a grid of equal squares in the tree's order, row by row, a gap apart, with the column count that makes the squares largest; room the grid leaves is blank. The padding and the gaps are shares of the box's side (8 and 6 at its side's text scale), so the layout is the same at any size. Siblings share one text scale, their side over 400 map units or the largest below it at which every sibling's whole label fits: a leaf's centered in its square, a parent's in a header band at most a quarter of its square. Siblings share one header band too, as tall as the tallest of their labels at that scale. Record counts size nothing.

A box with children MUST show its label in its header band at its top and hold its children below it, so no two siblings overlap and no child leaves its parent. A label's kind and ID line and its title each wrap on whole words, never inside one, and nothing is clipped: a leaf's label is centered in it, a parent's sits at the top left of its header band. Every drawn box shows its label (`LA-EXP-DS10`). A domain is a square there, with a small hexagon mark in its header (`LA-V93-R05` holds in the Tree view). The focus never changes the map, and filters hide boxes without moving the rest. No parent lines are drawn: holding is the parent link.

When the data changes, a change under a parent MUST re-lay only that parent's region (for a move, the old and the new parent's; `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R22`): every box outside it keeps its place, size and text scale, and existing siblings keep their reading order.

title: Camera framing
statement:
Depth N MUST frame the focus, its parent at the left edge for context, and its descendants down to N levels below it, every stage, folder and group counting as a level, as in a file explorer. Depth MUST NOT add siblings or ancestors further up to the picture it frames, though the map around it stays in view. Depth stays 1 to 3, and a group at the center counts levels the same way. The summary counts this framed picture. Focusing a node, by a click, the address, Back and Forward or the step keys, MUST move the camera only: it MUST frame the focus and the levels the depth shows below it to fill the open space the floating panels leave over the stage, with the parent's level kept in view in a strip at the left edge. That opening frame MUST take whole rows of the focus's level, its edges in the gaps between them, and end on the right in the gap before the next column. It MUST zoom in no further than frames the focus with its children's column at its widest (two fifths of the focus's width, after its gap) and the padding past it, the width left over going to the parent's strip: so a column narrowed by many children, or a narrow column next that leaves little gap to end in, never draws the focus's header larger, and it reads at the same size on screen however the levels below it grow (`LA-EXP-DS06`). What lies outside the focus's subtree is drawn faded by the focus fade (`LA-V93-R73`). The camera's zoom limits MUST let it frame the deepest leaf of a large product, which is very small against the product's box (`LA-EXP-DS06`), and fit the whole map on a phone: at most as far in as draws the map's smallest box 400 pixels on its shorter side, and never less than 256 times the map's units, so the limit grows with the map; a ten-thousandth at least. The framed levels MUST fit the open space; the depth decides only what is framed. When that frame would draw the focus's children's titles under 11 pixels on screen (about the app's small UI text, so a child's title reads comfortably; a Tree box's title is about a fifth of its height, `LA-EXP-DS06`, so a 6:1 child reads from about 55 pixels tall), the camera MUST frame the children's column at reading size instead: from the focus's right edge, the focus kept in view at the left edge (a strip of it at least, as the parent's level is in the focus's own frame, and whatever width is left over); whole rows of the focus's level, as many as keep the children reading, when its row fits the open space at that size, and else whole rows of its children from the first, as many as read; their edges in the gaps between rows and the right edge in the gap before the next column, as in the focus's own frame, and the levels the depth shows below the children running on to their right. At every depth the rule reads the focus's children, the level the walk steps into: making the deepest level read would frame a single child's column and drop the levels the depth asks for. A focus whose children read keeps its own frame. Should the width not let the children read, they are framed as large as it lets them be. The focus's strip in that frame MUST be wide enough for its label to read with its title at 11 pixels or more, as its children's, widened from the parent's strip as far as its label needs and at most to under half the open space's width, the children's column taking the rest. The camera MUST move there from the view as it is, including one the person zoomed or panned, in one smooth zoom and pan (zooming out only as far as the pan needs) on the shared motion (`--motion-speed`, `--motion-ease`, at most twice the speed for a long path); on a page's first picture, on a resize of the stage and under reduced motion it MUST go there at once. Free zoom and pan move the same camera, by one wheel rule on every stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace) that the person's Scroll to zoom sets (Appearance, `LA-PLT-A4`). With Scroll to zoom off, the default and Figma's convention, scroll (a mouse wheel or a two-finger trackpad swipe) MUST pan by the screen pixels it scrolled, down and across at once on a trackpad; Shift with scroll MUST pan sideways, a wheel's vertical scroll turned horizontal unless the browser already turned it; and Cmd or Ctrl with scroll MUST zoom about the pointer. With Scroll to zoom on, scroll MUST zoom about the pointer; Cmd or Ctrl with scroll MUST pan, down and across at once as a trackpad scrolls; and Shift with scroll MUST pan sideways, as with it off. Either way a trackpad pinch MUST zoom about the pointer (the browser sends a pinch as a scroll with Ctrl set, so it is told from Ctrl with scroll by whether the Control key is down), every zoom within the zoom limits and a line or page of scroll scaled to pixels; a scroll MUST keep the move it began with, pan or zoom, its momentum included, and a key pressed or let go during it that changes that move (Cmd or Ctrl, or Shift with Scroll to zoom on) MUST stop it, the rest of that scroll dropped until it pauses or a new scroll begins; a drag pans; panning never changes the zoom or the focus; and the zoom buttons zoom about the open space's middle; a gesture during a glide takes over from it, and the frame button and the `.` command frame the focus again.

The map MUST be drawn on a canvas, anew for each frame of the camera. A viewport MUST be kept in doubles, and every map point placed on screen in doubles relative to the camera's center, with no transform but the screen's pixel ratio, so a box deep in a large map is as steady at a deep zoom as at the top. Each label's lines MUST be drawn at their size in the map times the zoom, so text is crisp at any zoom whatever the map's range. A visually hidden layer of the drawn boxes, in the keyboard's order, MUST carry focus, Tab, the arrow keys, Enter and Escape, and each box's role and name for assistive technology, and the box it focuses is drawn with the focus ring. The pointer MUST find the box under it from the map's own outlines (a box's rectangle, a shape's polygon or rounded corners), the last drawn first, so a child drawn over its parent is found before it. In the Nested view, focusing a node by any of the ways `LA-EXP-DS09` lists MUST move the same camera, in the same glide, to frame the focus's box in the open space, within the padding and centered, within the camera's zoom limits (`LA-EXP-DS09`). The Nested camera frames the focus's box whatever the depth, so the depth control is off in the Nested view. The level of detail is `LA-EXP-DS10`'s: only boxes in view and at least 3 pixels on screen each way are drawn, each with its label, a parent before its children so a child is drawn over its parent, and a level that would take the drawing past 260 boxes is not drawn (its parents stand for it). The keyboard's order is the tree's, a parent before its children. The ERD stage's camera, framing a new picture and on the Fit command, MUST fit the bounding box of all its boxes, the faded ones included, inside a margin (`LA-V94-R06`); a soft vignette of the canvas's own background MUST soften its edges.

title: Level of detail
statement: The graph MUST draw only the nodes in view (with a tenth of the stage to spare each way) and at least 3 pixels tall on screen, and each frame MUST draw only what lies on the canvas: a box, a bar or a line wholly past an edge (with a margin its stroke reaches) is passed over. Every drawn node MUST carry its label, its kind and ID line and its full title wrapped on whole words, at its fixed size in the map (`LA-EXP-DS06`): whether a node is drawn never depends on whether its text can be read, and the focus and the depth decide only what the camera frames (`LA-EXP-DS09`). Each frame the canvas MUST draw each drawn node's shape, border and fill, and its label's lines at their map size times the zoom; a node whose title would be drawn under 5 pixels on screen, where no text can be read, MUST be drawn as a plain block, its fill and edge with no label, icons, badges or decoration (small text is read by zooming in, when it is drawn again). The fonts of a label's lines on screen MUST be worked out once per box and zoom, so a pan, which keeps the zoom, works none out again. A drawn node's children too small to draw MUST be one bar in their level for each run of them. Level by level from the roots, a level that would take the drawing past 260 boxes MUST be drawn as one bar per parent instead, so a product of tens of thousands of records stays within the performance budgets (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`, `LA-PLT-UC09-R13`). The keyboard's layer of drawn boxes (`LA-EXP-DS09`) MUST take what a glide passes over once, as it starts, and be trimmed when it ends, so no frame of the glide rebuilds it.

title: ERD lines
statement: The ERD map draws exactly one line for each `has_one` and `has_many` link between entities, and one dashed line for each entity and each aggregate that entity's fields reference by ID, ending at that aggregate's root. No line stands for anything else.

title: Key display
statement: Shows a binding as the platform shows it: on a Mac as the symbols ⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ in Apple's order ("⇧⌘P"), elsewhere as words joined by + ("Ctrl+Shift+P"). Names each single-chord binding for `aria-keyshortcuts` with the DOM's modifier names ("Control+Shift+P"), and leaves out a sequence, which it cannot express.

title: Contrast audit
statement: Works out the WCAG contrast of each text and control token on what it is drawn on, for a theme in a mode, and which pairs fall below AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls).

title: Window placement
statement: Places a window at its saved bounds; a saved place that is no longer on a connected screen gives way to a centered window, and a size larger than the largest screen shrinks to fit it, never below the minimum size.

title: Launch folder
statement: On launch, opens a folder named on the command line (unpacked or packed) or dropped on the Dock icon; else the most recent folder that still opens; else, run from Lathe's own repo, that repo; else asks for a folder.

title: Whole-ID matching
statement: Finds whether a text names an ID as a whole ID: `TL-LEND-INV05` is not found in `TL-LEND-INV050` or `TL-LEND-INV05-T`. Otherwise a test could seem to be named by a file that names another.

title: Allowed test levels
statement: Gives the run by levels each test kind allows, cheapest first: constraint test unit or integration; invariant and specification tests unit or integration; domain service test unit; policy test integration, service, system or browser; use case test service, system or browser; view test unit or browser; endpoint test service or system; flow test system or browser; integration test integration, service or system; pattern rule test and standard rule test any.

title: Source file tracing
statement: A source file is traced when a technical record names it, or names a folder holding it. Source files are what the source globs match, less tests, configs, generated files, build output and other products' folders.

title: Route normal form
statement: Gives a route in one form, however it is written, so a record's route and the code's compare: the path alone (a query string or fragment picks a state within a page, not another page), every parameter as `{}` whatever its name or syntax (`<id>`, `:id`, `{id}`, `[id]`, a template's `${id}`, a regular expression's group or one-segment class), no repeated slash and no trailing slash but the root's. `/tools/{toolId}/damage`, `/tools/:id/damage` and `/^\/tools\/(\d+)\/damage$/` are all `/tools/{}/damage`.

title: Test case reading
statement: Reads the test cases in a test file's text, as text and never by running it: each call of `it` or `test` (with the modifiers only, skip, todo, fails, fail, fixme, slow, concurrent, sequential, skipIf, runIf and each, and Playwright's test) whose name is a string or template literal, with its line and the names of the `describe` or `test.describe` calls around it, and the IDs, as whole IDs, that those names and their `each` rows name. Strings, template literals, comments and regular expressions are skipped. A name that is not a literal, a test made by a helper function, and other runners' forms are not read.

title: Serves reach
statement: Works out, from the rows on every load and never stored, the business outcomes each record serves: a record MUST serve an outcome exactly when a use case whose capability serves that outcome reaches it. A use case reaches its UC requirements, flows and steps; what its steps invoke (a command with its entity's aggregate, the specifications it checks, the domain services it calls and the events it raises with each policy hearing one and that policy's command; a query with its read model and the specifications it selects by); the views its steps happen in with their view requirements and the UI components that render or build them; the integrations its steps exchange with; the endpoints exposing what it reaches with their API requirements; and the rules of the patterns it or its domain follows. From what it reaches it reaches an aggregate's entities, invariants, storage requirements and the value objects its fields hold with their constraints; a read model's storage requirements, the aggregates it reads and its fields' value objects; what a specification reads; the technical records implementing each, the standard rules they meet, the tests under each, and a product's own records under or designing a reached one. A capability serves its own outcomes.
